section_summary: This section contains diplomatic despatches, intelligence reports, official correspondence, and scientific publications from 1945 to 1946 regarding agriculture in wartime and occupied Japan. It covers intelligence on farm operations, crop quotas, rural cooperatives, and severe fertilizer shortages in Gumma Prefecture, inquiries regarding the disposal of Japanese-owned plantations in the Philippines, and studies on post-war agricultural support capacity and land reclamation. The section concludes with the opening chapters of SCAP Natural Resources Section Report No. 59 surveying Japan's extensive agricultural experiment station network and its achievements in crop breeding and sericulture.

subfiles.about: The American Consulate General in Vladivostok reports that it cannot obtain current economic or food production information regarding Japan and Japanese-occupied areas.
subfiles.summary: Vladivostok Consulate General reports no current information available on Japanese agricultural production and food conditions, promising future updates.
subfiles.title: Request of Department of Agriculture for Current Information on Agricultural Production and the Food Situation in Japan and Japanese-Occupied Areas

subfiles.about: The American Embassy in Chungking forwards Dr. A. B. Lewis's intelligence report on farm operations in Gumma Prefecture.
subfiles.summary: American Embassy in Chungking transmits five copies of Dr. A. B. Lewis's intelligence report on Gumma Prefecture farm operations.
subfiles.title: Report on Farm Operations in Gumma Prefecture, Japan

subfiles.about: An intelligence report based on a prisoner-of-war interrogation detailing farm operations, crop yields, fertilizer rationing, rural organizations, and aircraft factories in Gumma Prefecture.
subfiles.summary: Based on interviews with prisoner of war M-921, this report describes farming operations, yields, grain quotas, and household rations on a landlord-tenant farm in Hosen-mura, Gumma Prefecture, during 1943-1944. It details wartime agricultural administration under the newly amalgamated Nogyo Kai, delivery requirements, warehouse fumigation, and severe commercial fertilizer shortages that curtailed crop production. It also records rural labor units, local tax burdens, and nearby industrial facilities including the Nakajima aircraft plant in Ota.
subfiles.title: Report on Farm Operations in Gumma Prefecture, Japan (Office Memo No. 219 / Report No. R-125-D-45)

subfiles.about: The State Department requests that W. I. Ladejinsky prepare a research paper analyzing post-war Japanese agricultural production and farm population capacity.
subfiles.summary: Haley requests that agricultural economist W. I. Ladejinsky prepare a study on post-war Japanese agriculture and farm population support.
subfiles.title: Request for Study on Japanese Agriculture

subfiles.about: Norman Orme inquires about establishing a commercial coconut dehydrating plant in the Pacific and asks about policy regarding abandoned Japanese-owned plantations.
subfiles.summary: Orme inquires about establishing a coconut dehydrating plant on Pacific islands and disposing of untended Japanese-owned plantations.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Disposal of Japanese-Owned Plantations and Coconut Dehydrating Plant

subfiles.about: The State Department replies to Norman Orme regarding Alien Property Custodian investigations of Japanese-owned plantations in Davao and Manila.
subfiles.summary: Ballantine informs Orme that the Alien Property Custodian is investigating Davao plantations and opening a Manila office for land disposal.
subfiles.title: Disposal of Japanese Owned Plantations in the Philippines

subfiles.about: The State Department sends copies of correspondence with Norman Orme concerning Japanese plantations in the Philippines to the American Mission in Haiti for delivery.
subfiles.summary: Transmits copies of correspondence with Norman Orme regarding Japanese-owned Philippine plantations for delivery through the mission in Port-au-Prince.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 406 Transmitting Correspondence with Norman Orme
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge of the American Mission, Port-au-Prince

subfiles.about: The State Department sends correspondence from Norman Orme to Manila consular officers, requesting a report on the disposal of Japanese plantations.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Orme correspondence to Manila consular officials, requesting an investigation and report on Japanese-owned plantation disposal.
subfiles.title: Instruction Concerning Norman Orme's Request on Japanese-Owned Plantations
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Manila

subfiles.about: Consul General Steintorf reports that the Alien Property Custodian is investigating Japanese plantation lands in Davao and preparing to establish a Manila office.
subfiles.summary: Steintorf reports Alien Property Custodian personnel are investigating Davao lands and opening a Manila office to handle illegal Japanese holdings.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 119: Mr. Norman Orme's Request for Information on the Disposal of Japanese-owned Plantations

subfiles.about: Clair Wilcox acknowledges receipt of W. I. Ladejinsky's research paper on post-war Japanese agriculture for the economic policy committee.
subfiles.summary: Wilcox acknowledges receipt of Ladejinsky's paper on Japanese agricultural population capacity for the committee on post-war economic policy.
subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Ladejinsky Paper on Japanese Agriculture

subfiles.about: F. A. Flood transmits W. I. Ladejinsky's paper analyzing whether Japanese agriculture can support a larger farm population.
subfiles.summary: Flood forwards W. I. Ladejinsky's study on Japanese agricultural support capacity to the State Department.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Paper: Can Japanese Agriculture Support a Larger Farm Population?

subfiles.about: A censored Domei news report outlines the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry's land reclamation program and machinery shortages.
subfiles.summary: Domei news copy reports Japanese government plans to reclaim millions of acres of land, facing tractor and land-acquisition shortages.
subfiles.title: Agriculture: Many Problems in Farm Expansion

subfiles.about: A National Archives notice certifying the withdrawal of a classified Civil Censorship Detachment intercept dated September 27, 1945.
subfiles.summary: Notice recording withdrawal of a security-classified Civil Censorship Detachment intercept dated September 27, 1945 from the file.
subfiles.title: Notice of Withdrawal of Classified Item 894.61/9-2745

subfiles.about: Milton I. Vanger requests information from the State Department regarding United States occupation policy on Japanese agriculture and farmer cooperatives.
subfiles.summary: Vanger requests information on United States occupation policy regarding agricultural democratization and farmer cooperatives for a Princeton conference.
subfiles.title: Inquiry on United States Occupation Policy Towards Japanese Agriculture

subfiles.about: Hugh Borton refers Milton I. Vanger to recent conferences between State Department officials and Princeton representatives regarding agricultural reform policy.
subfiles.summary: Borton refers Vanger to discussions held between Division officers and Princeton representatives on Japanese agricultural policy.
subfiles.title: Reply Concerning Policy Towards Japanese Agriculture

subfiles.about: A duplicate page of the Domei news article discussing land prices, tractor procurement, and acreage targets in Hokkaido.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate page of Domei press release detailing rising land prices, tractor procurement, and farm acreage targets in Hokkaido.
subfiles.title: Agriculture: Many Problems in Farm Expansion (Duplicate Page 2)

subfiles.about: A comprehensive preliminary report on the organization, facilities, and scientific achievements of Japanese agricultural experiment stations.
subfiles.summary: Prepared by Scientific Consultant S. C. Salmon for the SCAP Natural Resources Section, this preliminary report evaluates the extensive system of Imperial, prefectural, and private agricultural experiment stations across Japan. It examines station history, organization, staffing, educational functions, research methodologies, and budget allocations in relation to occupation goals of maximizing food production. The report highlights major scientific achievements, notably the breeding of high-yielding disease-resistant rice varieties and the revolutionary development of F1 hybrid silkworms and artificial hatching techniques.
subfiles.title: The Agricultural Experiment Stations of Japan (Report No. 59)
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
